I would urgently email payroll and any available HR decision-maker, marking the **12:00 deadline** and explaining that the code appears to trigger an automatic dismissal letter. I would ask whether the run or letter can be held for an authorised review, including a check for any applicable statutory protection. I would copy the HR Manager, but not rely on the manager or team leaders reading the message before noon.

Under the stated codes, Ryan’s absence is **UA**: he says he was not ill, and his sister does not fall within the specified dependant definition. His call matters, but UA covers any other unbooked absence, not just a failure to call. I would record the family emergency and his reported 05:40 call in a factual note.

If no authorised intervention arrives before payroll, I would correct SC to UA rather than knowingly submit a sickness code that is false. That means the stated process will send the dismissal letter today; the note alone cannot prevent it. I would make that consequence explicit in the escalation, rather than assume someone will catch it or that a later review will stop the letter.
